title: [test] remove defaultValue option not supported in node < v24
body: Node v24 added this option, the test actually expects the node v20 behavior of returning `undefined` which is the value in higher node versions when `defaultValue` is not set. This allows running tests in higher node versions.

title: [DevTools] Keep unmatched console specifiers literal in single-string formatter
body:
formatConsoleArgumentsToSingleString builds the message key for errors and warnings logged during render, commit and passive effects. Its replace callback always shifted an argument, even when none were left or when the specifier was escaped (%%s). With no argument left, a specifier became 'undefined' or 'NaN', so '%s %s' with one argument gave 'value undefined' and '%d %d' with one argument gave '1 NaN'. An escaped specifier also shifted an argument, coerced it and put it back, so '%%d %s' with 'abc' gave '%d NaN', and '%s %%s' with one argument appended ' undefined'.

Leave a specifier as is when it is escaped or when no argument is left, like the browser console, Node's util.format and the sibling formatConsoleArguments helper (fixed in #36930) already do.

Fixes #37126

title: buffer: limit UTF-8 fast calls to safe one-byte strings
body:
Alternative to https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/67134. This is a
standalone change against `main`; it does not depend on that PR.

Keep a fast UTF-8 byte-length path for sequential one-byte strings.
The fast binding's slow fallback returns the Smi sentinel `-1` without
reading or flattening the string. JavaScript then calls the regular
binding separately. Both the fast callback and its fallback avoid JS-heap
allocation; allocating string handling uses an ordinary API continuation.

Validation on Linux x64, GCC 14.2.0, release builds of v28.0.0-pre:

- Candidate `44bd1bfa65f`. The local regular-callback baseline
  `35cf29a820a` is main `250037174ee` with the removal fix from #67134,
  used only for the benchmark comparison.
- A negative control using a one-byte signature with an allocating slow
  fallback aborts both the direct and HTTP reproducers in 3/3 runs each.
- The candidate passes the direct reproducer 10/10 and HTTP 5/5. Traces
  show actual lazy deoptimization after weak objects are cleared, followed
  by normal completion, including `end()` and `maybePrepareFinalChunk()`.
- All 531 buffer, HTTP, string-decoder and snapshot tests pass, including
  explicit optimized fast-acceptance and rejection checks.
- Main thread, four workers, and a user-land startup snapshot pass the
  string-representation corpus before and after optimization.
- Additional GC stress, ESLint, focused binding type checking, cpplint,
  import, C++ formatting and whitespace checks pass.

Benchmark tradeoff versus the regular-callback baseline, ten alternating
runs per binary on one fixed logical CPU, two million calls per case:

| UTF-8 input | repeat=1 | repeat=16 | repeat=256 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| one-byte ASCII | +65.03% +/-12.95 | -9.70% +/-12.50 | -12.64% +/-6.43 |
| Latin-1 | +33.18% +/-10.41 | -7.12% +/-6.46 | -2.15% +/-5.28 |
| two-byte | -8.04% +/-4.37 | -7.07% +/-4.67 | -1.60% +/-5.64 |

Values are throughput changes with 95% confidence intervals in percentage
points. The repeated one-byte strings take the fallback. Eligible flat
inputs improve, while rejected inputs pay for the additional call.
Latin-1 and base64 encoding controls were also measured; raw results cover
27 configurations and 540 samples. Four comparisons remain significant
at 5% after the benchmark tool's Holm-Bonferroni adjustment.

```sh
./node benchmark/compare.js --old ./node-baseline --new ./node-candidate \
  --runs 10 --filter buffer-bytelength-string \
  --set encoding=utf8 --set encoding=latin1 --set encoding=base64 \
  --set type=one_byte --set type=latin1 --set type=two_bytes \
  --set repeat=1 --set repeat=16 --set repeat=256 --set n=2000000 \
  --set CPUSET=1 --no-progress --analyze --csv benchmark.csv buffers
```

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/66870

AI assistance: Codex helped prepare the implementation and tests.

title: Size new arena chunks from the previous chunk's capacity
body:
Arena.NewSlice computed the next chunk size from len(a.data), but it grows whenever the request does not fit in the remaining space, which usually happens before the current chunk is full. Doubling the used length rather than the chunk capacity could make the next chunk the same size as, or smaller than, the one being replaced. Arenas that mostly serve slices then kept allocating small chunks and never reached the intended steady-state size.

Base the growth on cap(a.data) so each chunk doubles the previous one up to the size ceiling. Arena.New only grows when len == cap, so it already behaved correctly; it now uses cap as well for consistency.

Thanks @teamchong for finding this!

title: fix: await overlapping plugin container close calls
body:
What is this PR solving?

The plugin container previously used only a `_closed` flag. Once the first `close()` call started, subsequent calls would return immediately, even if asynchronous plugin cleanup was still running

The fix stores the ongoing cleanup operation in `_closePromise`, so overlapping calls wait for the cleanup to finish. It also keeps `_closed` to prevent cleanup hooks from running more than once.

The regression tests use controlled promises to reproduce the timing issue They cover overlapping environment shutdown, the interaction between `environment.close()` and `server.close()`, and cleanup failures.

Codex assisted in implementing the patch and executing tests.I have reviewed the responsibilities of _closed and _closePromise

title: fix(dev): escape ANSI escape sequence for `server.forwardConsole`
body:
Any text sent from the browser was shown as-is in the terminal when `server.forwardConsole` was enabled.
Some terminals implements some features that controls other things by printing to the terminal. For example, OSC 52 allows modifying the clipboard content.

This PR prevents that by escaping content with those ansi escape sequences. It still allows colors that are supported by Chrome DevTools.

refs #20916

title: perf(javascript): escape strings, count name characters and find node tokens with less work
body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->

**Summary**

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->
<!-- Any other information related to changes. -->

Three hot spots a CPU and allocation profile of the JavaScript minifier found, each with output byte for byte the same:

- **String literals**: escaped in the loop that already counts their quotes, where a regexp called a function for every escape. A tab written raw is no longer escaped and then unescaped again.
- **Mangler character counts**: the source is counted once, then adjusted for each number printed in decimal. Before, it copied the whole source up to three times.
- **A node's tokens**: a node's start token is searched from the last start found. Before, it was searched from the parent's end, so it almost never hit the fast path.

Measured on `lodash.js` and `three.module.js`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| instructions per minify, three.js (callgrind, CodSpeed flags) | 8,106.9M | 8,043.1M (−0.79%) |
| instructions per minify, lodash | 4,222.9M | 4,205.9M (−0.40%) |
| allocated, lodash + three + acorn (sampling) | 41.6 MB | 38.6 MB (−7%) |
| token binary-search steps, three.js | 511K | 373K (−27%) |

Output check: the minify corpora report is unchanged, and 402 `node_modules` files give the same output under three option sets, including `ascii_only` and `ie8`.

No new changeset: the pending "minifies faster" entry covers this.

title: fix(javascript): print a function moved into one printed first where that one prints
body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->

**Summary**

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->
<!-- Any other information related to changes. -->

Minifying TypeScript's own `typescript.js` threw an error. The cause:

* A function declaration that is read once, before it is declared, prints at its read, so the walk prints it early.
* A function read once inside such a function is printed at that same early point, not at its own read.
* The check that every function it reads is already printed by then compared against the inner read's position. It should compare against where the outer function prints.

```js
// input
function f() { function w() { return b() } function a() { return x() } function b() { return c() } function c() { return a() } return w() }
```

| | output |
| --- | --- |
| before | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` |
| after | `function f(){function n(){return x()}return n()}` |

On `typescript.js` (9.1 MB), it now minifies to 3.5 MB. The minified file still transpiles and type-checks `lib.es5.d.ts` with 0 diagnostics. The minify corpora report is unchanged.

No changeset: the inlining this fixes (#22969) is not released yet.
